questions.q: What is the main function of the sepal in a flower?
questions.explain: The sepal protects the flower while it is still a bud.
procedure: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower
While the flower is still a bud, the sepal wraps around it
This protects the delicate inner parts from damage and weather
Once the flower opens, the sepal stays at the base
Answer: To protect the flower bud

questions.q: What is the coloured part of a flower called?
questions.explain: Petals are the bright, coloured parts of a flower.
procedure: Look at any flower — the colourful leaves you see are petals
Petals are usually bright and attractive
Their colour and scent attract insects and birds
Answer: Petal

questions.q: Which part of a flower produces pollen?
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of the flower and produces pollen.
procedure: The stamen is the male part of the flower
It has two parts: the anther and the filament
The anther at the top produces the yellow pollen grains
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: Which part of the flower receives pollen during pollination?
questions.explain: The stigma is the top of the pistil and receives pollen grains.
procedure: The pistil is the female part of the flower
Its top is called the stigma
The stigma is sticky, so pollen grains stick to it
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the male part of a flower called?
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of a flower.
procedure: Flowers have both male and female parts
The male part is called the stamen
It produces pollen, which contains the male sex cells
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: What is the female part of a flower called?
questions.explain: The pistil is the female part of a flower.
procedure: The female part of a flower is the pistil
It has three parts: stigma, style, and ovary
The ovary contains the egg cells (ovules)
Answer: Pistil

questions.q: Which part of the pistil contains the egg cells?
questions.explain: The ovary is at the base of the pistil and contains the egg cells.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma (top), style (middle), and ovary (bottom)
The ovary is the swollen base of the pistil
Inside the ovary are the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit
Answer: Ovary

questions.q: What is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma called?
questions.explain: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma.
procedure: Pollination = movement of pollen from anther to stigma
It can happen within the same flower or between flowers
Wind, insects, birds, and water can carry pollen
Answer: Pollination

questions.q: After pollination, what happens to the pollen grain on the stigma?
options: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.explain: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube down through the style to reach the ovary.
procedure: A pollen grain lands on the sticky stigma
It grows a long tube called the pollen tube
The tube grows down through the style to the ovary
The male sex cell travels down the tube to join the egg cell
Answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary

questions.q: What is formed when the male and female sex cells join?
questions.explain: The joining of male and female cells forms a seed.
procedure: Fertilization = when male and female cells join
The fertilized egg cell develops into a seed
The ovary around it becomes the fruit
Answer: A seed

questions.q: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit after fertilization?
questions.explain: After fertilization, the ovary grows into the fruit.
procedure: Before fertilization: the ovary holds the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization: the ovules become seeds
The ovary itself grows and becomes the fruit
This is why every fruit contains seeds
Answer: The ovary

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the stamen?
questions.explain: The stigma is part of the pistil, not the stamen.
procedure: Stamen = anther + filament (male parts)
Pistil = stigma + style + ovary (female parts)
The stigma belongs to the pistil, not the stamen
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the anther called?
questions.explain: The filament is the thin stalk that holds up the anther.
procedure: The stamen has two parts: anther and filament
The anther is at the top — it holds pollen
The filament is the thin stalk that supports the anther
Answer: Filament

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the stigma called?
questions.explain: The style is the tube that connects the stigma to the ovary.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma, style, ovary
The stigma is at the top
The style is the middle tube that connects stigma to ovary
Answer: Style

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way pollen can be transferred?
questions.explain: Pollen is transferred by wind, insects, birds, or water — not electricity.
procedure: Pollination happens through natural agents
Wind carries light pollen grains
Insects and birds carry pollen as they visit flowers
Water can carry pollen in some water plants
Electricity is not a pollinating agent
Answer: Electricity

questions.q: Why are petals usually brightly coloured?
options: To make the flower look nice for humans
To attract insects and birds for pollination
To protect the flower from rain
To help the flower grow taller
questions.answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination
questions.explain: Bright petals attract pollinators, which help the flower reproduce.
procedure: Many flowers need insects or birds to carry pollen
Bright colours and pleasant scents attract these pollinators
The pollinators come for nectar, but leave with pollen on their bodies
They carry the pollen to the next flower
Answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination

questions.q: Which part of the flower is usually green and found at the base?
questions.explain: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower.
procedure: Look at a flower from the outside
The green, leaf-like parts at the bottom are sepals
They protect the flower bud before it opens
Answer: Sepal

questions.q: What do flowers produce that we often enjoy for their beauty and smell?
questions.explain: Flowers produce nectar and scent that attract pollinators.
procedure: Flowers make nectar (a sweet liquid) inside them
They also release scent through their petals
Both are used to attract insects and birds
Nectar also provides food for the pollinators
Answer: Nectar and scent

questions.q: A bee visits a flower and later visits another. What is the bee doing?
questions.explain: The bee carries pollen from one flower to another.
procedure: As a bee collects nectar, pollen sticks to its hairy body
When it visits the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off onto the stigma
This transfer is called pollination
The bee is helping the flowers reproduce
Answer: Pollinating the flowers

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of the flower's life from bud to seed?
options: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.explain: The flower grows from a bud, opens, gets pollinated, fertilized, and produces fruit and seeds.
procedure: 1. Bud forms (protected by sepals)
2. Bud opens into a flower with petals
3. Pollination happens (pollen reaches stigma)
4. Fertilization happens (sex cells join)
5. Ovary becomes fruit, ovules become seeds
Answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed

questions.q: What is the water cycle?
options: Water moving through pipes in a house
The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air
questions.answer: The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air
questions.explain: The water cycle is the never-ending movement of water on Earth.
procedure: The water cycle is also called the hydrological cycle
Water moves between the oceans, the sky, and the land
It changes form: liquid → gas → liquid
This movement never stops
Answer: The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air

questions.q: What is it called when water changes from liquid to gas?
questions.explain: Evaporation is when water changes from liquid to gas (water vapour).
procedure: The sun heats water in oceans, rivers, and lakes
When water is heated enough, it changes into water vapour (a gas)
This process is called evaporation
You can see it when puddles dry up on a hot day
Answer: Evaporation

questions.q: What is the main source of energy that drives the water cycle?
questions.explain: The sun provides the heat energy that powers the water cycle.
procedure: The water cycle needs energy to keep going
That energy comes from the sun
The sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers
This causes evaporation to happen
Answer: The sun

questions.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid?
questions.explain: Condensation is when water vapour cools and becomes liquid water.
procedure: Water vapour rises into the sky
As it goes higher, the air is colder
The cool air makes the water vapour turn back into tiny droplets
This process is called condensation
Answer: Condensation

questions.q: What do we call the tiny water droplets that form in the sky?
questions.explain: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets that form from condensation.
procedure: When water vapour condenses high in the sky, it forms tiny droplets
Millions of these droplets together form clouds
Clouds look white or grey depending on the light and thickness
Answer: Clouds

questions.q: What is it called when water falls from clouds as rain, hail, or snow?
questions.explain: Precipitation is water falling from clouds to the ground.
procedure: Cloud droplets grow bigger and heavier
When they become too heavy, they fall as precipitation
Precipitation can be rain, hail, or snow
Answer: Precipitation

questions.q: What is transpiration?
options: Water moving from soil to plant roots
Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air
questions.answer: Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air
questions.explain: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plants.
procedure: Plants take in water through their roots
Some of this water travels up to the leaves
The leaves release extra water as vapour into the air
This release is called transpiration
Answer: Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of the water cycle?
questions.explain: Electricity is not part of the water cycle.
procedure: The main stages of the water cycle are: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
Transpiration is also part of the cycle
Electricity is not involved in the water cycle
Answer: Electricity

questions.q: Where does the water that falls as rain go?
options: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes
questions.answer: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes
questions.explain: Rainwater is collected in the ground, rivers, lakes, and oceans.
procedure: When rain falls, some water sinks into the ground
Some water flows over the land into streams and rivers
Rivers carry the water into lakes and oceans
This step is called collection
Answer: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes

questions.q: Why is the water cycle important for life on Earth?
options: It makes the sky look pretty
It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans
questions.answer: It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans
questions.explain: The water cycle gives us a constant supply of fresh water.
procedure: All living things need water
The water cycle moves water from the oceans to the land as rain
Plants, animals, and humans use this fresh water
The cycle keeps repeating, so water is never used up
Answer: It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans

questions.q: Which state of matter is water vapour?
questions.explain: Water vapour is water in its gas form.
procedure: Water can exist in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), gas (vapour)
Water vapour is the gas form of water
It is invisible — you cannot see water vapour directly
Answer: Gas

questions.q: When you boil water in a pot, what do you see rising?
questions.explain: Steam rises when water is heated — that's water vapour.
procedure: When water is heated, it changes into gas
The gas rises as steam
The white mist you see is actually tiny water droplets that form when steam hits cooler air
This is a real-life example of evaporation and condensation
Answer: Steam (water vapour)

questions.q: Why does wet ground dry up faster on a sunny day?
options: Because the sun drinks the water
Because the heat makes water evaporate faster
Because wind blows the water away
questions.answer: Because the heat makes water evaporate faster
questions.explain: Heat from the sun speeds up evaporation.
procedure: Evaporation happens all the time, but faster when it's hot
The sun heats the wet ground
The heat gives water molecules energy to escape as vapour
So the water dries up faster on a sunny day
Answer: Because the heat makes water evaporate faster

questions.q: Where does most evaporation happen on Earth?
questions.explain: Oceans cover most of Earth, so most evaporation happens there.
procedure: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth's surface
Because they are so large, most evaporation happens there
The sun heats the ocean surface, causing water to turn into vapour
Answer: In the oceans

questions.q: What causes rain to fall from clouds?
options: The clouds open up like doors
Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall
The moon pulls the rain down
questions.answer: Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall
questions.explain: When cloud droplets combine and become heavy, they fall as rain.
procedure: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets
Droplets bump into each other and join together
They grow bigger and heavier
When they become too heavy to float, they fall as rain
Answer: Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall

questions.q: Which process returns water to the sky from plants?
questions.explain: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plant leaves.
procedure: Plants absorb water through their roots
Some water is used for food-making (photosynthesis)
The rest is released as vapour through small holes in the leaves
This release is called transpiration
Answer: Transpiration

questions.q: If we cut down too many trees, how does it affect the water cycle?
options: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns
questions.answer: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns
questions.explain: Fewer trees means less transpiration and less moisture in the air.
procedure: Trees release water vapour into the air through transpiration
This vapour helps form clouds and rain
When many trees are cut down, less vapour is released
This can lead to less rainfall in the area
Answer: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns

questions.q: Which of these is a good way to conserve water?
options: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car
questions.answer: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car
questions.explain: Using a bucket uses much less water than a running hose.
procedure: Water conservation means using less water
A hose can waste many litres per minute
A bucket uses only a few litres total
Small choices save a lot of water over time
Answer: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car

questions.q: What happens to water when it freezes?
questions.explain: When water freezes, it becomes solid ice.
procedure: Water exists in three states: solid, liquid, gas
When water cools below 0°C, it freezes
It becomes solid ice
When it warms up again, it melts back to liquid water
Answer: It becomes a solid (ice)

questions.q: Which of the following is a real-life example of condensation?
options: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass
questions.answer: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass
questions.explain: Water vapour in the air cools on the cold glass and turns into droplets.
procedure: A cold glass makes the air around it cool
Water vapour in the air touches the cold glass
The vapour cools and turns into liquid droplets
This is condensation — the same process that forms clouds
Answer: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass
